Check a copy of the engine of inlavanilla

Source: R/vendor-status.R
vanilla_status.Rd

Checks the copy of the engine that use_vanilla() put into the package whose root is path, and prints one line per check: a tick when it passes, a cross when it fails, and an exclamation mark for something to look at, each with what to do. The checks, in this order:

  • Lock: inst/inlavanilla.lock exists and can be read.

  • Copies: each engine file has the MD5 hash in the lock, and every file R/vanilla-*.R is in the lock. The hash is taken after carriage returns are removed, so that a checkout with Windows line endings passes.

  • Names: no object of an engine file is also defined in another file of R/, or imported by name in NAMESPACE. R keeps one of the two with no warning, so a clash breaks the engine or your code silently.

  • Dependencies: DESCRIPTION has cli (>= 3.6.0), stats and utils in Imports (or Depends), future and parallelly in Suggests (or above), and asks for R 4.1.0 or later.

  • Authors: Authors@R names the copyright holders of the engine, with the role "cph".

  • License: the package's License allows code under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later.

  • Release: the release in the lock is a tag on GitHub at the commit in the lock, and each engine file at that tag has the hash in the lock.

  • Update: no newer release of inlavanilla changes a copied file. A newer release that does is reported, with the command that updates the copy, and is not a failure.

The last two checks need GitHub, or a local clone of inlavanilla given as clone. Without either they are skipped with a note, and the others still run.

Usage

vanilla_status(path = ".", clone = NULL, error = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The root of the package, or a folder inside it. By default the working directory.

clone

The path of a local clone of inlavanilla, for the last two checks without the internet. It needs git, and its tags must be up to date (git fetch --tags). By default they use GitHub.

error

If TRUE, stop with an error when a check fails, as continuous integration needs. A skipped check or an exclamation mark is never an error.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with a row per check, in the order above: check ("lock", "copies", "names", "dependencies", "authors", "license", "release" or "update"), status ("pass", "warn", "fail" or "skip"), message, the line printed for it, and details, the lines printed under it, as plain text.

See also

use_vanilla() to copy and update the engine, and use_vanilla_ci() to run these checks on GitHub.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# From the root of a package that holds a copy of the engine
vanilla_status()

# In continuous integration: an error when a check fails
vanilla_status(error = TRUE)
} # }
